t: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, an officer of the Navy in the Supply Corps or the Civil Engineer Corps who is not selected for promotion to a higher grade after the enactment of this Act may not be retired under chapter 573 of title 10, United States Code, earlier than he would have been retired had this Act not been enacted.

fable.w: This is a savings provision protecting the retirement timing of Navy officers who are not selected for promotion. There is no tempting reading here: it involves only federal military personnel and creates no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving parties outside the federal government.
fable.s: an officer of the Navy in the Supply Corps or the Civil Engineer Corps who is not selected for promotion to a higher grade after the enactment of this Act may not be retired under chapter 573 of title 10, United States Code, earlier than he would have been retired had this Act not been enacted.

qwen_block.w: This section establishes eligibility criteria for the retirement of federal employees (Navy officers). It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are federal officials and employees, and the action is an internal personnel matter.
qwen_block.s: an officer of the Navy in the Supply Corps or the Civil Engineer Corps who is not selected for promotion to a higher grade after the enactment of this Act may not be retired under chapter 573 of title 10, United States Code, earlier than he would have been retired had this Act not been enacted.

opus.w: The section only limits when certain Navy officers who are passed over for promotion can be retired. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision. Promotion and retirement under title 10 happen entirely within the federal government, and the officers are federal employees, so nothing here is participation.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning:** The tempting reading is that a rule about promotion and retirement involves some decision process that outsiders take part in. That reading fails. The section only protects Navy Supply Corps and Civil Engineer Corps officers from being retired earlier than they would have been before this Act. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section concerns the retirement eligibility of federal employees (Navy officers). The definition states that federal employees are inside the federal government, and participation requires involvement of parties outside the government. There is no consultation, hearing, or coordination with non-federal entities involved in this decision.
qwen_chat.s: an officer of the Navy in the Supply Corps or the Civil Engineer Corps who is not selected for promotion to a higher grade after the enactment of this Act may not be retired under chapter 573 of title 10, United States Code, earlier than he would have been retired had this Act not been enacted.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the officer has a "right" to remain in service, which could be seen as a form of participation or protection. However, this is an internal personnel matter regarding federal employees (Navy officers). The definition explicitly states that federal employees are INSIDE the federal government. There is no consultation with, or coordination involving, any party outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in making the decision about retirement eligibility. The section merely sets a rule for when a federal employee can retire.
